name: Fix Book
office_task: Keep the fixes our techs find on site, and when a tech asks how we fixed a fault before, show them what was written on that job, or tell them we have no record.
systems_of_record: the job system that issues the job_id and names the tech on each job (ServiceM8, Simpro, Tradify, Fergus), whose id names each job's fix folder on the drive
the shared drive that holds the fix notes, voice memos, service manuals and procedures and issues the document_id (Google Drive or SharePoint), left where it is
the register on that tenant (one Sheet or SharePoint list: a row per source, owner a person, kind, edition and checksum)
the task list the office runs (Google Tasks, Planner or a sheet), which issues the exception_id for each open question

emits.write: the tech's fix, sent back after the job, filed as one fix note (fault, cause, fix, parts, tested) into Fixes/<job_id>/ on the drive by the job system's job_id, with the customer's name, phone and address left out; it is then registered with the tech as owner before any of it is searchable
emits.readback: the drive returns the note's file id, and reading that id back returns the note in the job_id's folder with the message_id it came from; no id back means nothing was filed and the tech's message is raised to the service manager

emits.write: a task on the office's task list naming the person who owns it, with a due date: a fix note or procedure whose only owner is a team, two copies of one fix note waiting for a person to pick the one to keep, a customer's material waiting for someone to set who may read it and for how long, a manual or fault code chart the office expects and the drive does not hold, a tech's message with no fault or no fix line, or a registered file gone from the drive
emits.readback: the task list returns an exception_id, and reading that id back returns what is expected, the owner and the due date; no id back means nothing was raised, and the file stays off the index
